title: The Vision of God
author: Nicholas of Cusa (Salter trans)
description: The Vision of God (De visione Dei) by Nicholas of Cusa (1401-1464), translated by Emma Gurney Salter with an introduction by Evelyn Underhill (1928). Written in 1453 for the Benedictine monks of Tegernsee, the treatise accompanied a painted 'all-seeing' icon whose eyes seem to follow every viewer. Cusanus asks the monks to experience how the gaze rests on each of them at once, and from this exercise develops a meditation on God's seeing as God's being and creating. In twenty-five chapters addressed in prayer to God, he explores the coincidence of opposites as the 'wall of paradise' beyond which God dwells, infinity, love, the Trinity, and Jesus as the consummation in whom the divine and human are united. A jewel of late medieval mystical theology, it joins Dionysian apophaticism with a new perspectival vision and is a key bridge to Renaissance thought.
